name: Crab Nebula
description: Remnant of a supernova observed in 1054 AD. Contains the Crab Pulsar — a rapidly spinning neutron star and one of the first identified pulsars.

name: M2
description: One of the largest known globular clusters at 175 light-years across, containing about 150,000 stars.

name: M3
description: Bright globular cluster containing roughly 500,000 stars; one of the most studied in the sky.

name: M4
description: One of the closest globular clusters to Earth at about 7,200 light-years, located near the bright star Antares.

name: M5
description: One of the largest and oldest known globular clusters, estimated at 13 billion years old, containing hundreds of thousands of stars.

name: Butterfly Cluster
description: Open cluster whose stars are arranged in a pattern resembling a butterfly with open wings, located in the tail of Scorpius.

name: Ptolemy Cluster
description: Bright open cluster recorded by Ptolemy in 130 AD; visible to the naked eye in the tail of Scorpius.

name: Lagoon Nebula
description: Large emission nebula and active star-forming region about 4,100 light-years away, visible to the naked eye under dark skies.

name: M9
description: Globular cluster about 25,800 light-years away, located near the galactic center.

name: M10
description: Globular cluster about 14,300 light-years away, with a dense core and broad outer halo of stars.

name: Wild Duck Cluster
description: Rich open cluster containing about 2,900 stars; its V-shape resembles a flock of ducks in flight.

name: M12
description: Loosely concentrated globular cluster about 15,700 light-years away, sometimes called the 'Gumball Globular'.

name: Hercules Globular Cluster
description: Brightest globular cluster in the northern sky, containing several hundred thousand stars about 22,200 light-years away.

name: M14
description: Globular cluster about 30,300 light-years away, containing more than 150,000 stars.

name: M15
description: One of the densest globular clusters known, containing a rare planetary nebula and possibly a central black hole.

name: Eagle Nebula
description: Star-forming region famous for the 'Pillars of Creation' imaged by Hubble Space Telescope, about 7,000 light-years away.

name: Omega Nebula
description: Bright emission nebula also known as the Swan or Horseshoe Nebula, an active region of star formation.

name: M18
description: Sparse open cluster containing about 20 stars, located between M17 and M24.

name: M19
description: One of the most oblate globular clusters known, located about 28,700 light-years away.

name: Trifid Nebula
description: Combination emission and reflection nebula divided into three lobes by dark dust lanes; an active star-forming region.

name: M21
description: Young open cluster about 4,250 light-years away, containing about 57 stars.

name: Sagittarius Cluster
description: One of the brightest globular clusters visible from Earth, about 10,400 light-years away.

name: M23
description: Open cluster containing about 150 stars, located approximately 2,150 light-years away.

name: Sagittarius Star Cloud
description: Dense Milky Way star cloud rather than a true cluster, providing a window through galactic dust to thousands of distant stars.

name: M25
description: Bright open cluster about 2,000 light-years away, containing the Cepheid variable star U Sagittarii.

name: M26
description: Open cluster about 5,000 light-years away, containing roughly 90 stars.

name: Dumbbell Nebula
description: First planetary nebula ever discovered, named for its dumbbell-shaped appearance through small telescopes.

name: M28
description: Globular cluster about 17,900 light-years away; the first cluster found to contain a millisecond pulsar.

name: M29
description: Small open cluster of about 50 stars in the rich Milky Way star fields of Cygnus.

name: M30
description: Dense, core-collapsed globular cluster about 27,100 light-years away.

name: Andromeda Galaxy
description: Closest large spiral galaxy at 2.5 million light-years; the most distant object visible to the naked eye and on a collision course with the Milky Way.

name: M32
description: Compact dwarf elliptical satellite galaxy of the Andromeda Galaxy.

name: Triangulum Galaxy
description: Third-largest member of the Local Group at about 2.7 million light-years; one of the most distant objects visible to the unaided eye under dark skies.

name: M34
description: Open cluster of about 100 stars, visible to the naked eye under good conditions.

name: M35
description: Large, bright open cluster containing several hundred stars, easily visible with binoculars.

name: M36
description: Young open cluster of about 60 stars, similar in age to the Pleiades.

name: M37
description: Richest of the Auriga open clusters, containing more than 500 stars.

name: M38
description: Open cluster about 4,200 light-years away, with stars arranged in a cross or pi-shaped pattern.

name: M39
description: Loose, bright open cluster of about 30 stars, easily visible with binoculars.

name: Winnecke 4
description: Optical double star mistakenly cataloged by Messier as a nebula; the two stars are unrelated and at different distances.

name: M41
description: Bright open cluster about 2,300 light-years away, containing approximately 100 stars including several red giants.

name: Orion Nebula
description: Brightest nebula in the night sky and the closest large star-forming region at 1,344 light-years; contains the Trapezium Cluster of young stars.

name: De Mairan's Nebula
description: Part of the Orion Nebula complex, separated from M42 by a dark dust lane.

name: Beehive Cluster
description: Also known as Praesepe; one of the closest open clusters to Earth at 577 light-years and visible to the naked eye.

name: Pleiades
description: The Seven Sisters; brightest and most famous open cluster, easily visible to the naked eye and surrounded by reflection nebulosity.

name: M46
description: Rich open cluster of about 500 stars, with the planetary nebula NGC 2438 superimposed in front.

name: M47
description: Bright, loose open cluster about 1,600 light-years away, containing roughly 50 stars.

name: M48
description: Large open cluster of about 80 stars, visible to the naked eye under dark skies.

name: M49
description: Brightest member of the Virgo Cluster of galaxies; a giant elliptical containing about 200 billion stars.

name: M50
description: Open cluster about 3,200 light-years away, containing roughly 200 stars in a heart-shaped pattern.

name: Whirlpool Galaxy
description: Iconic face-on grand-design spiral galaxy interacting with its smaller companion NGC 5195; the first galaxy in which spiral structure was identified.

name: M52
description: Rich open cluster of about 200 stars, located near the Bubble Nebula.

name: M53
description: Globular cluster about 58,000 light-years away, one of the more distant globulars in the Messier catalog.

name: M54
description: First globular cluster discovered to belong to another galaxy; part of the Sagittarius Dwarf Galaxy.

name: M55
description: Loose globular cluster about 17,600 light-years away, easily resolved into individual stars.

name: M56
description: Globular cluster about 32,900 light-years away, located in a rich Milky Way star field.

name: Ring Nebula
description: Iconic planetary nebula formed by a dying star ejecting its outer layers; one of the most photographed deep-sky objects.

name: M58
description: Barred spiral galaxy in the Virgo Cluster, located about 62 million light-years away.

name: M59
description: Elliptical galaxy in the Virgo Cluster, notable for an unusual counter-rotating core.

name: M60
description: Massive elliptical galaxy in the Virgo Cluster, hosting one of the most massive supermassive black holes known.

name: M61
description: Barred spiral galaxy in the Virgo Cluster, notable for hosting numerous observed supernovae.

name: M62
description: One of the most irregularly shaped globular clusters, possibly distorted by tidal forces from the galactic center.

name: Sunflower Galaxy
description: Flocculent spiral galaxy with many short, fragmented arms resembling sunflower petals.

name: Black Eye Galaxy
description: Spiral galaxy with a prominent dark dust lane in front of its bright nucleus, resembling a black eye.

name: M65
description: Member of the Leo Triplet of galaxies, a nearly edge-on spiral about 35 million light-years away.

name: M66
description: Largest member of the Leo Triplet, with asymmetric spiral arms distorted by gravitational interactions with neighbors.

name: M67
description: One of the oldest known open clusters at about 4 billion years; useful for studying stellar evolution.

name: M68
description: Globular cluster about 33,600 light-years away in the southern constellation Hydra.

name: M69
description: Compact globular cluster about 29,700 light-years away, with one of the highest metal contents among globulars.

name: M70
description: Globular cluster about 29,300 light-years away, similar in appearance to its near-neighbor M69.

name: M71
description: Loosely concentrated globular cluster, once thought to be an open cluster due to its sparse appearance.

name: M72
description: Faint, distant globular cluster about 54,600 light-years away.

name: M73
description: Group of four stars in a Y-shaped asterism with no physical association; an unusual non-cluster Messier entry.

name: M74
description: Face-on grand-design spiral galaxy about 32 million light-years away; considered one of the most difficult Messier objects to observe due to low surface brightness.

name: M75
description: Compact, distant globular cluster about 67,500 light-years away, one of the most concentrated in the catalog.

name: Little Dumbbell Nebula
description: Planetary nebula resembling a smaller version of the Dumbbell Nebula (M27); among the faintest Messier objects.

name: M77
description: Active barred spiral galaxy and the closest, brightest example of a Seyfert galaxy with an active nucleus.

name: M78
description: Brightest reflection nebula visible from Earth, illuminated by hot young stars within the Orion Molecular Cloud Complex.

name: M79
description: Globular cluster about 41,000 light-years away, possibly originating outside the Milky Way galaxy.

name: M80
description: Densely concentrated globular cluster about 32,600 light-years away; site of a rare nova outburst in 1860.

name: Bode's Galaxy
description: Bright grand-design spiral galaxy about 12 million light-years away; one of the brightest galaxies visible from Earth and an excellent target for small telescopes.

name: Cigar Galaxy
description: Edge-on starburst galaxy with intense star formation triggered by gravitational interaction with M81; ejects superwinds visible in red H-alpha light.

name: Southern Pinwheel Galaxy
description: Bright face-on barred spiral galaxy about 15 million light-years away, prolific in supernova production.

name: M84
description: Lenticular or elliptical galaxy in the Virgo Cluster, with a supermassive black hole at its center.

name: M85
description: Lenticular galaxy at the northern edge of the Virgo Cluster, about 60 million light-years away.

name: M86
description: Lenticular galaxy in the heart of the Virgo Cluster, notable for its rapid blueshifted approach toward the Milky Way.

name: Virgo A
description: Supergiant elliptical galaxy at the center of the Virgo Cluster; hosts the supermassive black hole that was the first ever directly imaged by the Event Horizon Telescope in 2019.

name: M88
description: Beautifully symmetric spiral galaxy in the Virgo Cluster, with multiple well-defined spiral arms.

name: M89
description: Nearly perfectly spherical elliptical galaxy in the Virgo Cluster, surrounded by a faint envelope of gas and dust.

name: M90
description: Spiral galaxy in the Virgo Cluster, blueshifted and approaching the Milky Way as it falls toward the cluster center.

name: M91
description: Barred spiral galaxy in the Virgo Cluster; the faintest galaxy in the Messier catalog.

name: M92
description: Bright globular cluster about 26,700 light-years away; often overlooked due to its proximity to the more famous M13.

name: M93
description: Open cluster of about 80 stars, located approximately 3,600 light-years away.

name: M94
description: Spiral galaxy with a bright inner ring of intense star formation around a luminous nucleus.

name: M95
description: Barred spiral galaxy in the Leo I group, about 38 million light-years away.

name: M96
description: Brightest member of the Leo I group; an asymmetric spiral with a small bar and dust lanes.

name: Owl Nebula
description: Planetary nebula whose two dark patches resemble owl eyes; about 2,030 light-years away.

name: M98
description: Nearly edge-on spiral galaxy in the Virgo Cluster, about 44 million light-years away.

name: M99
description: Face-on grand-design spiral in the Virgo Cluster with asymmetric arms distorted by gravitational interactions.

name: M100
description: Bright face-on grand-design spiral and one of the most prominent members of the Virgo Cluster.

name: Pinwheel Galaxy
description: Large face-on spiral galaxy about 21 million light-years away, with prominent asymmetric spiral arms and many giant H II regions.

name: Spindle Galaxy
description: Edge-on lenticular galaxy (NGC 5866), with a prominent dust lane bisecting the nucleus; identification as M102 has been historically debated.

name: M103
description: Small fan-shaped open cluster of about 25 stars, one of the most distant open clusters in the Messier catalog.

name: Sombrero Galaxy
description: Edge-on spiral with a brilliant central bulge encircled by a thick prominent dust lane resembling a Mexican hat; about 29 million light-years away.

name: M105
description: Elliptical galaxy in the Leo I group, harboring a supermassive black hole of about 200 million solar masses.

name: M106
description: Spiral galaxy with anomalous extra arms revealed by an active galactic nucleus; one of the closest active galaxies.

name: M107
description: Loose globular cluster about 20,900 light-years away, with several dark obscured regions.

name: Surfboard Galaxy
description: Nearly edge-on barred spiral galaxy with mottled dust lanes, about 46 million light-years away.

name: M109
description: Barred spiral galaxy and the most distant Messier object at about 83 million light-years from Earth.

name: M110
description: Dwarf elliptical satellite galaxy of the Andromeda Galaxy; the last object added to the Messier catalog.
